records.title: Make document quality review evidence-backed
records.summary: Use the Site for reusable methods and a source-grounded brief for each application. Treat integrity, chronology, and extraction as prerequisites to judging reader and document quality.
records.question: How should document quality be reviewed without mistaking cosmetic polish or approval labels for evidence?
records.decision: Expand the existing editorial Skills, reconcile Leah and Sofia, use a small content trial, and require version-specific independent findings before a review can pass.
records.rationale: A resume audit found changed attribution and action verbs, weakened context, cosmetic variations, and approval labels without inspectable review evidence. The process is adopted; its effect on the next resume remains untested.
records.alternatives: Another full visual redesign; a universal resume score; additional Personas; an app-managed runtime. Start with existing capabilities and a bounded trial.
records.tradeoffs: Claim tracking and concrete findings take more care. Focus them on consequential claims and affected checks; do not add a general approval ritual to every edit.
records.affects: Skills, Leah, Sofia, job-search handoffs, Docs, and the isolated resume editorial trial.
records.revisit: A real trial still produces generic or misleading content, the reviewer cannot find evidence, or the process creates effort without improving the reader’s understanding.

records.title: Flow hierarchy for Persona work
records.summary: Organize each person’s work into foundational, supporting, and edge-case flows, with the activity inventory embedded inside each flow.
records.question: Should the Persona page follow a day, a list of activities, or the outcomes the person is trying to produce?
records.decision: Use flow hierarchy as the primary structure. Each tier can contain multiple workflows.
records.rationale: This keeps cadence, tools, priorities, friction, and recovery work attached to the context where they matter.
records.affects: Persona cards, Persona detail views, and the persona-research guidance.
records.evidence: Layout Lab prototype and current Docs guidance.
records.revisit: Real Persona research shows that users need a different first-order way to compare work.

records.title: Operating Packs are contextual library space
records.summary: Catalog reusable, file-based operating context alongside the existing library spaces while keeping actual Markdown source outside the catalog when appropriate.
records.question: Where should domain or project instructions, standards, conventions, procedures, references, and validation guidance live when they are reusable but not executable capabilities?
records.decision: Add Operating Packs as a first-class space with a small source/location record, explicit availability, and scoped Persona, Skill, workflow, Playbook, and Tool-use relationships.
records.rationale: Contextual rules need a durable home that does not turn Skills into project instruction or Playbooks into duplicated policy. Scoped applications keep a pack relevant to the work where it applies.
records.tradeoffs: The catalog does not transport or execute packs, and external references may remain planned or unavailable until verified. Project conventions remain local unless later evidence supports broader reuse.
records.affects: Orientation routing, Docs, Site navigation, the Operating Pack catalog, lifecycle Skills, and reconciliation guidance.
records.revisit: A pack needs executable runtime behavior, repeated rules reveal a generalizable Skill, a Playbook duplicates pack content, or external source transport becomes a separately authorized product need.

records.title: Templates are reusable starting artifacts
records.summary: Add Templates as a first-class library space beside Operating Packs while preserving a distinct ownership boundary for reusable starting structure.
records.question: Where should reusable starting structures and scaffolds live when they accelerate work but do not define how the work should be performed?

records.title: Template Librarian stewards the collection
records.summary: Add a library-stewardship Persona for Template discoverability, provenance, lifecycle, and routing while keeping substantive Template quality with domain specialists.
records.question: Who keeps the Template collection organized and trustworthy without becoming the domain expert for every artifact?
records.decision: Use the Template Librarian to maintain catalog identity, source verification, duplication control, promotion, deprecation, relocation, and reconciliation. Route discipline-specific research and composition to the relevant specialist.
records.rationale: Library stewardship and domain judgment are different kinds of work. Keeping them separate preserves the Template boundary and lets the collection grow without turning one Persona into a polymath.
records.affects: Template routing, Persona workflows and handoffs, Template lifecycle Skills, Docs, generated Persona output, and reconciliation. Mara Okoye remains the escalation point for architecture and concept-boundary questions.
records.evidence: Template Librarian Persona, Templates catalog, Templates guidance, and issue #63.
records.revisit: Observed Template work shows that stewardship and domain composition cannot remain separate, a dedicated reusable capability is justified, or external artifact ownership changes.

records.title: Bounded parallel implementation is a distinct Playbook
records.summary: Keep Multi-Persona Collaboration as named-Persona synthesis through a shared problem-context. Catalog bounded parallel repository implementation as its own Playbook with Coordinator, Implementer, Reviewer, and Authorizer roles.
records.question: Should usage-conscious parallel implementation be a new Playbook or a profile of Multi-Persona Collaboration, especially while #71 is still open?
records.decision: Add playbook-bounded-parallel-implementation as a distinct Playbook. Reference collaboration instead of copying its stages, solution-quality gate, or problem-context contract. Do not create an Agent, Coordinator, Runtime, Budget, or Scheduler entity.
records.rationale: Collaboration produces one inspectable solution from Persona lenses. Bounded parallel implementation produces independent reviewable PRs with one-level delegation, compact GitHub-reference handoffs, independent review, and separately authorized merge. Those outcomes and gates are materially different.
records.alternatives: Extend Multi-Persona Collaboration with an implementation profile; wait for #71 before adding identity; encode ChatGPT Work or Codex as canonical meaning. Rejected because they mix synthesis with mutation gates or bind the contract to a runtime.
records.affects: Playbook catalog, Playbooks orientation route, Site Playbooks and Docs surfaces, root AGENTS.md activation, and Work Order evidence for #82. Collaboration methodology is unchanged.
records.evidence: Issues #71, #82, #86, #89, and #94 plus the bounded-parallel Work Order.
records.revisit: #71 catalogs collaboration identity, a two-repository proof is needed, or runtime-specific procedure becomes substantial enough for a Tool package.
corrections: 2026-09-14: The Playbook models four roles—Coordinator, Implementer, Reviewer, and Authorizer. Authorizer remains a role. Bounded-parallel activation lives on the Playbooks route group, not as an always-on root AGENTS.md rule.

2026-09-14: Source-grounding is a required stage of the same Playbook identity, not a second Playbook. The target repository owns implementation truth after selection; Persona-Library remains catalog and discovery. Contradicted work stops for re-scope. Root AGENTS.md still does not carry bounded-parallel procedure. See issue #86.

2026-09-14: Issue #71 catalogs playbook-multi-persona-collaboration as its own first-class identity, resolving to the existing docs/collaboration/multi-persona-collaboration-playbook.md contract without copying its stages or gate. The two Playbooks remain distinct as decided above.

2026-09-14: The live-proof extension adds an orientation preflight before source-grounding and a bounded completion callback adapter. Implementer context remains fresh, previously_oriented, or unknown; grounding remains confirmed, qualified, or contradicted. Callback packets are notification-only, GitHub remains review truth, unsupported transport uses a compact coordinator fallback, and independent review, scoped correction/re-review, and separately authorized merge remain unchanged. See issues #89 and #94.

records.title: Riley is the default routing front door
records.summary: Riley Morgan is the default interaction and routing front door for unqualified requests while Playbooks retain procedural ownership and specialists retain domain judgment.
records.question: How should an unqualified request enter the Persona Library when the work may be narrow specialist work or a larger reusable outcome?
records.decision: Riley interprets intent and selects the smallest useful route: narrow work may go to a specialist or Skill; outcome-scale work may go to a Playbook; a bounded consultation, Tool path, or other focused route may be selected when that is the smallest useful fit. Explicit requests naming a specialist, Skill, or Playbook may route directly without an artificial Riley hop.
records.rationale: Issue #90 correctly removed job-search domain ownership from Riley, but its front-door wording also made the Evidence-led Job Search Playbook appear to be the default entry. Separating entry/routing ownership from procedural and domain ownership restores the intended interaction model without adding a runtime router or moving expertise.
records.alternatives: Keep the Playbook as the universal front door; make Riley own the complete job-search method; add a routing service or registry. Rejected because these options either force taxonomy-first interaction, transfer specialist judgment, or add unnecessary runtime architecture.
records.tradeoffs: Riley must choose among routes without absorbing their expertise. The route contract needs explicit tests and should be revisited if observed requests consistently choose a larger or less capable path than the smallest useful route.
records.affects: docs/job-search/implementation.md; content/orientation/docs.json; Riley’s authored record and maintenance history; routing validators/tests; generated library and Decisions output; issue #111.
records.evidence: Issue #111, PR #112, the Riley Persona/workflow sources, the four explicit routing tests, and Mara’s placement review recorded in the issue-111 Work Order.

records.title: Personas operate Playbooks; job search gets a domain orchestrator
records.summary: Keep Riley Morgan as the default routing front door for unqualified requests, then use Priya Desai · Job search orchestrator as the operating Persona for full-outcome Evidence-led Job Search. Treat Playbooks as process surfaces rather than autonomous actors.
records.question: After Riley routes an unqualified request, who exercises judgment and remains responsible for a full Playbook run when the Playbook itself is a process surface rather than an actor?
records.decision: Riley remains the default system entry and routing point for unqualified requests. A Persona operates a Playbook. For full-outcome job search, Riley routes to job-search-orchestrator / Priya Desai; Priya operates playbook-evidence-led-job-search. The Playbook defines stages, shared state, handoffs, quality gates, recovery, and learning but does not independently exercise judgment or own the outcome. Explicit requests for Priya, a specialist, a Skill, or the Playbook may route directly.
records.rationale: DEC-013 restored Riley as the default routing front door. Issue #113 addresses a separate layer: DEC-011 also gave the Playbook actor-like outcome ownership. A dedicated domain orchestrator fills that operating role without transferring specialist expertise into Riley or into the Playbook.
records.alternatives: Keep the Playbook as actor/owner; make Riley the job-search domain operator; stretch Elena into end-to-end orchestration. Rejected because each option blurs an existing responsibility boundary.
records.tradeoffs: The architecture gains one additional Persona and routing hop for unqualified full-outcome job-search work. In return, entry/routing, process operation, process structure, and specialist judgment remain explicit and independently testable.
records.affects: Architecture; Playbook composition guidance; Riley/Priya job-search routing; Evidence-led Job Search docs and Site surfaces; Docs orientation; job ledger orchestration wording; application Work Order fields; generated validation; issue #113.
records.evidence: Issue #113, PR #114, canonical Priya Persona/workflows/Skill applications, the Riley-first routing contract from DEC-013, and focused validation.

records.title: A designated candidate baseline preserves the career spine
records.summary: When current standing decisions designate a private master or baseline resume, resolve it before role tailoring. Reusable Templates and normalized resume models remain separate layers and must not silently reconstruct the candidate's approved career spine.
records.question: How should reusable Templates and normalized resume content interact with an explicitly promoted private candidate master?
records.decision: Add Candidate Baseline Resume as a private Candidate Context layer. Standing decisions determine whether one is active. Resolve the exact baseline source and revision before resume composition, use it as the default composition baseline for the protected career spine, keep evidence authoritative for factual truth, keep reusable Templates authoritative only for reusable presentation structure, and use normalized resume content as an optional portability layer. Material protected-field changes require a verified evidence correction or explicit candidate decision; intentional material omissions are recorded as omitted_with_reason; an unresolved designated baseline blocks the affected resume composition.
records.rationale: The 2026-09-18 Tessera Labs packet bypassed the candidate's active standing decisions and Google Docs master, then reconstructed the resume from stale or secondary context. That run dropped recent employers, changed chronology and contact data, weakened quantified evidence, and produced a materially different ATS artifact. The September 16–17 Candidate Context, Resume Content Model, and semantic Template mapping work separated reusable structure from candidate data correctly but left the promoted private baseline implicit rather than first-class.
records.alternatives: Remove the reusable Template and Resume Content Model architecture; promote the private master into the reusable Template library; or always regenerate role resumes from evidence/model data. Rejected because the first loses useful reusable infrastructure, the second leaks candidate-specific composition into a reusable artifact boundary, and the third repeats the failure mode this decision is intended to prevent.
records.tradeoffs: Application runs gain one explicit private-source resolution step and one baseline-to-output integrity comparison. That adds a small amount of process state, but it prevents silent loss of approved candidate chronology and structure while preserving the ability to use materially different verified Templates when needed.
records.affects: docs/job-search/implementation.md; docs/job-search/candidate-context-contract.md; docs/job-search/candidate-context-integration.md; docs/job-search/resume-template-mapping.md; docs/job-search/application-work-order-template.md; .agents/skills/resume-template-semantic-mapping/SKILL.md; content/orientation/docs.json and generated route data; validation guards/tests; Candidate Application Context Operating Pack; issue #148.

records.revisit: A future candidate explicitly replaces the baseline with a different source-of-truth model, repeated runs show baseline drift creates more conflicts than it prevents, or a validated normalized candidate model becomes the explicitly designated composition baseline through a later candidate decision.

records.title: Application tracking stays private and extractable
records.summary: Add a top-level Applications surface while keeping real opportunity and application records browser-local, portable, and independent of canonical Persona and Skill data.
records.question: How can Persona Library support application tracking now without publishing private job history or making a later standalone app difficult to extract?
records.decision: Ship application tracking as a separate top-level Applications companion surface. Persona Library owns the tracker code, portable record schema, lifecycle vocabulary, and export/import behavior; real application records remain browser-local private state and never become canonical repository data. Keep seen-job deduplication, candidate context, and application lifecycle tracking as separate contracts.
records.rationale: The requester wants application tracking inside Persona Library now but may make Persona Library public later or split the tracker into its own app. Coupling records to Persona/Skill data or committing opportunity history would create a privacy problem and an expensive extraction boundary. Browser-local persistence provides useful single-user state while versioned JSON keeps the data portable.
records.alternatives: Store application records in Git; overload the seen-job deduplication contract; embed lifecycle state directly into the job-search Playbook page; or build a separate app immediately. Rejected because they respectively expose private history, collapse distinct state models, couple persistence to orchestration presentation, or add infrastructure before it is needed.
records.tradeoffs: Browser-local storage is single-device and can be lost when browser data is cleared, so export is the backup and migration path. In return, the repository stays publishable, the MVP needs no backend or authentication, and a future standalone app can replace only the storage adapter rather than untangling canonical library records.
records.affects: Top-level Applications Site surface; build/navigation; docs/job-search/application-tracker-contract.md; job-search implementation and candidate-context boundaries; architecture; generated validation; issue #151.
records.evidence: Requester decision on 2026-09-18; public Persona-Library repository boundary; existing private candidate-context and seen-job contracts; issue #151; WO-2026-09-18-job-application-tracker.
records.revisit: Application tracking needs authenticated cross-device sync, collaboration, external integrations, or server-side automation; browser-local recovery proves insufficient; or extraction into a standalone app begins.
records.status_note: Superseded by DEC-017 after application tracking required authenticated cross-device and agent-accessible persistence. DEC-016 remains the historical MVP boundary.

records.title: Authenticated storage becomes primary for private application tracking
records.summary: Keep Persona-Library as the code and contract owner while moving real opportunity rows behind an authenticated Supabase storage adapter; preserve Git as canonical authoring for library catalogs.
records.question: Where should private application state live now that browser-local persistence prevents reliable cross-device and authorized agent updates, and should the same database become the canonical home for Persona-Library catalogs?
records.decision: Use authenticated Supabase storage as the primary opportunity store when configured. Persona-Library owns the tracker UI, portable schema, storage adapter, database contract, and migration/export behavior, but real opportunity rows remain private operational data outside Git. Keep browser-local state only as an explicit fallback, migration source, and rollback copy; never silently redirect a failed remote write to local storage. Keep Personas, Skills, Tools, Templates, Operating Packs, Playbooks, Docs, Decisions, and Work Orders canonical in Git. Any later Supabase catalog tables are deterministic read-only projections from those authored sources, not a replacement authoring system.
records.rationale: The local-only MVP protected privacy and extraction, but it prevents ChatGPT/Codex workflows from reliably creating or updating tracked opportunities and does not provide cross-device persistence. A storage adapter preserves the extraction boundary while authenticated RLS-backed storage solves the operational requirement. Keeping catalog authoring in Git retains reviewable diffs, provenance, validation, and deterministic builds while still allowing a future query index.
records.alternatives: Keep localStorage and rely on import/handoff files; store opportunity history in Git; repurpose an unrelated existing Supabase project; move all canonical catalogs into database tables; or split Applications into a separate app immediately. These respectively preserve the integration constraint, violate privacy, blur project ownership, weaken Git-based authoring/provenance, or add extraction work before the storage boundary is proven.
records.tradeoffs: The tracker now depends on authentication, deployment configuration, RLS, and an external service when remote mode is enabled. Local fallback/export remains important for recovery. Catalog projection adds synchronization responsibility later, so it is deferred until opportunity persistence is proven.
records.affects: Applications storage/runtime, build configuration, docs/job-search/application-tracker-contract.md, architecture, validation, issue #156, future catalog projection, and the later disposition of issue #153.
records.evidence: Requester direction on 2026-09-19; issue #156; current browser-local integration constraint; current Supabase documentation for publishable browser clients, custom Data API schemas, Auth, explicit grants, and RLS; WO-2026-09-19-supabase-opportunity-store.
records.revisit: Authenticated persistence creates unacceptable operational cost or security burden; the tracker is extracted into a standalone application with a different private store; or evidence shows canonical catalog authoring should move away from Git.

records.title: Remote tool work batches evidence, CI, and review checkpoints
records.summary: Separate repository validation from deployed-state verification: reuse still-valid remote evidence, batch coherent changes, use GitHub CI for repository correctness, and reserve Vercel Preview for materially user-reviewable or deployment-specific states.
records.question: How should increasingly autonomous agents keep repository work safe and visible without making remote calls, commits, CI runs, and Vercel deployments scale with every internal iteration?
records.decision: Use the Tool-use layer to require bounded evidence gathering, explicit freshness triggers, coherent batching, and cheapest-sufficient validation. GitHub is the default remote repository truth and CI validation surface; refresh it when evidence can materially change and immediately before consequential mutations. Vercel is the deployed-state verification surface: non-main intermediate commits are skipped by default, while agents deliberately create or allow a Preview for materially new user-reviewable states or questions that repository CI cannot answer. Keep Production deployment from main separate and consequential.
records.rationale: Live Vercel inspection for issue #159 found at least 20 Persona-Library deployments in roughly 35 minutes, including four errors, while no grouped production runtime errors were found in the inspected seven-day window. The commit sequence showed validation and diagnostic iterations repeatedly reaching deployment infrastructure. Reducing only Vercel builds would leave the broader remote-call pattern intact, while suppressing previews entirely would make work harder to steer.
records.alternatives: Buy more Vercel capacity; continue deploying every intermediate commit; disable previews entirely; or encode the behavior separately in every Persona and workflow. Rejected because these respectively mask the cause, preserve churn, reduce visibility, or duplicate vendor-specific execution guidance.
records.tradeoffs: Agents must distinguish still-valid evidence from freshness-sensitive state and decide when a review checkpoint is materially useful. CI becomes a required repository validation layer, and Preview triggering gains a small amount of infrastructure logic. In return, remote cost and noise should fall without removing reviewability or safety.
records.affects: Tool discovery/safe execution guidance; GitHub and Vercel Tool-use recipes; Riley Tool requirements; repository AGENTS guidance; Work Order guidance; GitHub Actions validation; Vercel ignored-build configuration; issue #159.
records.evidence: Issue #159; live Vercel deployment inspection on 2026-09-21; Persona-Library commit/deployment history; current Tool-use architecture and repository validation contracts.
records.revisit: Representative workstreams miss deployed defects, users receive review checkpoints too late to steer effectively, GitHub CI becomes materially more expensive than the avoided deployment churn, or Vercel/GitHub platform behavior changes the safe trigger model.

records.title: Scoped implementation requests carry standing completion authorization
records.summary: For Persona-Library, a scoped request to implement, fix, build, or complete repository work authorizes the normal implementation path through merge once current completion gates pass, unless the requester explicitly narrows the stopping boundary.
records.question: Should Persona-Library require a second user confirmation to merge after a requester has already asked it to implement scoped repository work and the current PR has passed review and validation?
records.decision: Treat a scoped requester instruction to implement, fix, build, or complete Persona-Library work as standing completion authorization for branch/file changes, pull-request creation and updates, scoped review corrections, and merge into the default branch after fresh preflight. Explicit requester instructions such as `do not merge`, `PR only`, `leave for review`, or equivalent override the standing authorization. The standing rule is repository-specific and does not authorize unrelated issue mutation, repository settings/access changes, external repositories, external communications, or other out-of-scope consequential actions.
records.rationale: The canonical GitHub Tool contract already allows merge when either the requester or repository contract authorizes it. Requiring an additional chat confirmation after every green implementation creates a redundant gate without adding new scope or safety. Safety comes from a clearly bounded initial request, independent review, required validation, fresh merge preflight, and explicit override handling—not from repeating the same approval after the work is complete.
records.alternatives: Keep a mandatory second merge confirmation; change the reusable GitHub Tool contract for every repository; infer merge permission from green CI alone; or auto-merge every open PR. Rejected because they respectively add redundant friction, broaden a Persona-Library-specific preference globally, confuse validation with authorization, or remove the scoped-request boundary.
records.tradeoffs: Agents must preserve the exact original scope and requester overrides through the implementation lifecycle and must stop when current merge preflight exposes a blocker or out-of-scope side effect. In return, ordinary scoped implementation work can finish without an unnecessary conversational round trip while retaining fresh-state and review gates.
records.affects: AGENTS.md; docs/playbooks/bounded-parallel-implementation.md; content/orientation/playbooks.json and generated mirror; docs/work-orders.md; focused governance validation; future Persona-Library Work Orders; issue #172.
records.evidence: Requester direction on 2026-09-21; current rickvang/tool-repo GitHub contract revision 01198019e8f1520eb222dc6af2ec17bd81bc9c30; issue #172; prior issue #165/PR #166 consolidation of GitHub authorization semantics.

records.title: Authenticated storage becomes the durable seen-job set
records.summary: Keep seen-job deduplication separate from Applications while moving repeated-search memory into a dedicated authenticated Supabase table in the existing private application-data project.
records.question: Where should durable seen-job memory live now that repeated job-discovery runs need reliable suppression across sessions and authorized agent contexts, without turning Applications into a discovery-history ledger?
records.decision: Use the existing authenticated `persona-workspace-data` Supabase project with a dedicated private `app.seen_jobs` table as the durable seen-job store. Persona-Library owns the reusable stable-identity behavior, browser storage adapter contract, database schema/migration, and validation; real seen-job rows remain private operational data outside Git. Read the owner-bound store before presenting results and insert only jobs actually presented afterward. Prefer provider/source plus stable provider job ID, then canonical source URL, then a conservative normalized company + title + location fingerprint. Do not silently fall back to local storage. Keep this store separate from `app.opportunities`, which remains the Applications lifecycle store.
records.rationale: The earlier job-ledger boundary correctly kept private search history out of Git, but leaving the durable set only in a consuming runtime makes repeated searches unreliable across sessions and authorized agent contexts. DEC-017 already established authenticated Supabase with RLS as the private operational-state pattern for Applications. Reusing that project while creating a dedicated table preserves privacy and the separation between 'already shown' discovery memory and intentionally tracked opportunity lifecycle state.
records.alternatives: Keep the seen-job set only in caller memory or browser-local state; reuse `app.opportunities`; add seen/rejected/expired lifecycle fields to Applications; create a new Supabase project; or store seen-job history in Git. Rejected because they respectively fail durable cross-run suppression, conflate discovery with application lifecycle, expand the wrong state model, create unnecessary infrastructure, or violate the private-data boundary.
records.tradeoffs: Repeated-search deduplication now depends on authenticated Supabase availability, RLS, and the existing private project. There is intentionally no silent local fallback, so an unavailable remote store must be surfaced rather than forking deduplication history. In return, the identity and privacy boundary is durable, testable, and reusable across authorized job-discovery runs.
